_about: Machine readable plan of the Actually Additions backport onto the unreleased 1.20.1 base, in the state of the release of 2026-11-06. plan.bundles and plan.excluded are the plan after the review in critic_notes, and each bundle carries its status with the commits of okf/modpack/actuallyadditions-backport.md. plan.features holds the 67 features of the first draft with their upstream commits, paths and tests, each with the bundle of the final plan (bundle_in_first_draft names the draft bundle where the review moved it). meta and savegame_summary come from the first draft too, and their hours and bundle counts predate the review. Paths under bp2/ and aacritic/ are in the workflow scratchpad and are not in the repo. Handed on items are in actuallyadditions-backport-carryover.json.

base.state: Snapshot of the day the 1.20.4 port started: 121 blocks and 112 items registered, 131 lang entries labelled (wip), 109 generated recipes (main 204), no forge: tags, no worldgen (gen/AAWorldGen.java fully commented out), no village house or villager, no global loot modifiers, a manual item that opens nothing, laser relay tiles that call I18n, client to server packets that trust the client.

meta.version_recommendation: ActuallyAdditions-1.20.1-1.1.52-skytekx.1.jar with mod version 1.1.52-skytekx.1. Keep the 1.1.52 base number and state the content level (upstream 1.3.26 cd9d9c63 minus the exclusions) in UPSTREAM.md and NOTICE. A 1.3.26 base number would claim parity with a NeoForge 1.21.1 build that has data components and would send bug reports to the wrong changelog. No pack mod checks the version.
meta.integrations: No pack mod depends on Actually Additions. Patchouli 1.20.1-85-FORGE (manual, optional at runtime as upstream treats it since 19cfbc92), Curios 5.14.1 (charm slot for the crafting table on a stick), JEI 15 plus EMI 1.1.24-skytekx.2 (categories through EMI's JEI layer), Immersive Engineering 10.2.0-183 (cloche recipes), Mekanism 10.4.16 (energy relay fix, crushing compat, mining lens ores), Farmer's Delight 1.3.4 (shares forge:crops/rice). AlmostUnified 0.11.0: black quartz and the crystals are not AU materials, AA ships no dust, ingot or nugget, crushing outputs are vanilla raw ores, so nothing gets unified. Do not tag tiny coal as forge:nuggets/coal.
meta.skylands: Biome modifiers use #minecraft:is_overworld and forge:is_hot, is_cold, is_dense and is_sparse overworld tags. skytekx3:sky_void is only in skytekx3:has_structure/sky_floaters and the two Dungeons Arise tags, so no AA ore or plant lands over the void. Check with tools/void_scan.py on a pregenerated copy.
meta.arclight: Verified by javap on the Arclight 1.0.6 safeiter2 mod jar: BlockBreakEventDispatcher.onBreakBlock turns a posted Forge BlockEvent.BreakEvent into a Bukkit BlockBreakEvent with the fake player's CraftPlayer and copies the cancel back, BlockPlaceEventDispatcher.onBlockPlace does the same for EntityPlaceEvent when the entity is a ServerPlayer, BlockItemMixin fires BlockPlaceEvent for fake.gameMode.useItemOn placements, ArclightFakePlayer is the CraftPlayer of a Forge FakePlayer. EssentialsX is the only plugin today, no claim plugin or claim mod is installed. Upstream gaps: base Breaker posts no event, Phantom Breaker never does (even on main), reconstructor lenses set blocks directly, all use the shared [Minecraft] fake player and leave tools in its hand. Ticking risks: laser relay network lookup is linear per call, the magnet ring scans every tick, phantom blocks read their target block entity before the range check. No mixin of the fork touches a method Bukkit rewrites.
meta.method: Per bundle, cherry pick the upstream commits through the translated patch pipeline (port-patch-pipeline) onto ports/actuallyadditions, translate the NeoForge parts by hand with 63fbbb33 as the reverse map, mirror every provider change in src/generated by hand, one fix(actuallyadditions) or feat(actuallyadditions) commit per feature with the upstream hashes in the body.
meta.calibration: 261.5 h for 67 features, 3.9 h per feature, the rate of the Create Crafts & Additions inventory (136.5 h for 34 features). The Twilight Forest backport averaged 7.8 h per feature (about 1040 h for 133) but its features were merged worldgen and boss systems. The research estimate of about 120 h assumed 'build it and pick fixes'. The base turned out to be a work in progress snapshot, so most of the 1.20.4 port completion (about 7.8k added Java lines between 63fbbb33 and the 1.20.4 tip) has to be redone on 1.20.1.

bundles.spec:
[dedicated-server-client-split, 8 h] On the base, BlockPhantom, BlockLaserRelay, BlockAtomicReconstructor, BlockPlayerInterface, BlockVerticalDigger, BlockLavaFactoryController and ItemBooklet implement IHudDisplay with a displayHud(GuiGraphics, Minecraft, ...) method, the laser relay tiles import net.minecraft.client.resources.language.I18n and build their mode strings with I18n.get, and PacketHandler holds the client handlers that call Minecraft.getInstance(). Also live and touched by the split: ItemCoffee.MilkIngredient.getExtraText calls I18n.get in a common method (ItemCoffee.java:161, replaced by coffee-machine-and-coffee), util/StringUtil and util/AssetUtil mix client methods into common utility classes, UpdateChecker (only its @OnlyIn onTick touches client code, fine). 668f7ffe moves the HUDs into IBlockHud plus client only classes (LaserRelayHud, LavaFactoryControllerHud, MinerHud, PhantomHud, later FarmerHud) registered from ClientEvents. 844efe42 moves the goggles client tick and the client packet handlers out of common classes. 0226078a, 3a767e18 and d64b530f replace I18n with Component.translatable in common code. a20c25eb guards the Patchouli page registration. Upstream ties this to dedicated server crashes with Lithium (#1434). The same verifier class loading hits Arclight's dedicated server when a common class merges a client type in a stack map frame. Curios calls (ItemCrafterOnAStick in main imports CuriosApi in the common item) go into a separate compat class that only runs when ModList says curios is loaded.
Upstream commits: 668f7ffe, 844efe42, 8fd9afe8, 0226078a, d1ceffca, 3a767e18, d64b530f, a20c25eb.
Files (on the base or new): mod/blocks/IHudDisplay.java, mod/blocks/IBlockHud.java, mod/blocks/blockhuds/, mod/items/ItemEngineerGoggles.java, mod/network/PacketHandler.java, mod/network/PacketHandlerClient.java, mod/event/ClientEvents.java, mod/tile/TileEntityLaserRelay*.java, mod/util/StringUtil.java, mod/util/AssetUtil.java.
Translation: The 1.21 PacketHandlerClient and ClientPayloadHandler become a client only class called through DistExecutor.unsafeRunWhenOn(Dist.CLIENT) from the SimpleChannel consumer. Keep @OnlyIn(Dist.CLIENT) off interfaces that common classes implement. RegisterGuiOverlaysEvent or RenderGuiOverlayEvent drives the HUDs on 1.20.1.
Savegame: none.
New ids: none.
Test: javap -c over every class outside the client packages of the built jar: no net/minecraft/client reference outside methods that carry @OnlyIn(Dist.CLIENT) or classes only reached through DistExecutor. Dedicated Arclight server: place, wrench and right click every AA block, use every AA item, no NoClassDefFoundError and no 'invalid dist' crash.

[packet-hardening, 6.5 h] Local deviation, upstream main still trusts the client (ServerPayloadHandler.handleButtonToTile and siblings read dimension, pos and playerId from the packet). On the base (PacketHandler.java:92-171) GUI_BUTTON_TO_TILE, GUI_NUMBER_TO_TILE, GUI_STRING_TO_TILE and GUI_BUTTON_TO_CONTAINER take WorldID, X, Y, Z and PlayerID from the packet: any client can press buttons on any AA machine in any dimension as any player, load chunks through getBlockEntity, throw a NullPointerException with an unknown WorldID and a ClassCastException when PlayerID names a non player. PLAYER_DATA_TO_SERVER edits the player data of any UUID. Second hole: DATA_HANDLERS is one list for both directions (PacketHandler.java:195-203) and PacketClientToServer.fromBytes accepts any index (PacketClientToServer.java:39), so a client can send the index of a client handler (LASER_HANDLER, TILE_ENTITY_HANDLER, SYNC_PLAYER_DATA, LASER_PARTICLE_HANDLER). On the dedicated server their handleData carries @OnlyIn(Dist.CLIENT) and is stripped, so the call throws AbstractMethodError, and on a LAN host it runs client code with the guest's NBT (TILE_ENTITY_HANDLER feeds readSyncableNBT of the host's client level). Fix: (1) a serverbound allow list (the four GUI handlers, PLAYER_DATA_TO_SERVER, and the later hotkey and item tag handlers) checked in PacketClientToServer, a clientbound allow list in PacketServerToClient. (2) The sender (context.getSender()) is the only player, the dimension must be the sender's level, the position must be loaded (hasChunkAt) and within 8 blocks (64 square) or belong to the menu the sender has open, PlayerID and WorldID are ignored. (3) PLAYER_DATA_TO_SERVER: after c8e90aef its only effect is setDirty (main ServerPayloadHandler.handleSyncPlayer has every type branch commented out), so it becomes a no op that keeps its index. (4) Each reactor clamps its own values: the firework box ranges live in TileEntityFireworkBox.onNumberReceived and readSyncableNBT since the review fix of this bundle (UPSTREAM.md source change 17), the XP solidifier buttonID lower bound waits for xp-solidifier, the digger, ranged collector and sack menus already ignore unknown button ids. (5) Exceptions inside enqueueWork vanish in the CompletableFuture today: add exceptionally() with a WARN line naming the player (main disconnects the player instead). Since the review fix the WARN lines are limited to 20 per sender in 60 seconds. Bump PROTOCOL_VERSION from 4 to 5 once, here. Later bundles of this backport append handlers (hotkey, item tag) without another bump because no build ships in between.
Upstream commits: 9d166ac9 (only its split of client and server handlers).
Files (on the base or new): mod/network/PacketHandler.java, mod/network/PacketClientToServer.java, mod/network/PacketServerToClient.java, mod/network/PacketHelperServer.java.
Translation: Keep the SimpleChannel actuallyadditions:main and the NBT carrying PacketClientToServer format, so the client side code does not change shape. 9d166ac9 (1.21 networking overhaul into typed payloads) is not ported as such.

New ids: none.
Test: A dev only client command in a separate source set that the jar does not contain (KubeJS cannot send AA serverbound packets) sends crafted packets: a button press on a machine 20 blocks away, one in another dimension, a foreign PlayerID, an unknown WorldID, the index of each client handler and a PLAYER_DATA_TO_SERVER with another UUID. None has an effect, the server logs one WARN each and keeps running. A stock 1.1.52 client gets a clean protocol mismatch disconnect (not run yet, UPSTREAM.md source change 14 marks it not verified).

[menu-open-and-validity, 2 h] Both cited commits are already in effect on the base: f2596f97 feeds the block position into openMenu, which the base already does through NetworkHooks.openScreen(player, tile, pos) (BlockContainerBase.java:55 and the oil generator, coffee machine, canola press and fermenting barrel blocks), and 82aaacf1 only replaces worldPosition by getBlockPos() in canPlayerUse, which returns the same field. The real work is local: ContainerDrill, ContainerFilter and ContainerFireworkBox return true from stillValid. Drill upgrade dupe: ContainerDrill reads the upgrades from inventory.getSelected() at open and writes them back to inventory.getSelected() in removed() (ContainerDrill.java:130-136, unchanged on main). A client that sends a ServerboundSetCarriedItemPacket while the menu is open changes the selected slot, so on close the remaining upgrades are written into a second drill while the first keeps its old NBT with every upgrade the player took out. Fix: remember the slot index and the ItemStack at open, stillValid returns false once the selected index or the stack identity changed, removed() writes only into that remembered stack. Upstream fixes the drop path (902e8064, e91c1569) and the Breaker (main TileEntityBreaker:112), but the Phantom Breaker still breaks without any event and even computes the drops at its own position with its own block entity (main TileEntityPhantomPlacer.doWork: Block.getDrops(state, level, this.worldPosition, level.getBlockEntity(this.worldPosition))), and the Atomic Reconstructor conversion lens (MethodHandler.invokeConversionLens) and the mining lens set blocks with level.setBlock. Local fix: an AAFakePlayers helper around FakePlayerFactory.get(serverLevel, PROFILE) with a fixed GameProfile ([ActuallyAdditions], a constant UUID). Forge 47 caches one such player per level and profile, installs its FakePlayerNetHandler (FakePlayer.java:85) and drops it in unloadLevel, so the helper keeps no strong reference across a level unload. Each use positions the player at the machine and clears its hands afterwards. Every break goes through fireFakeHarvestEventsForDropChance (posts BlockEvent.BreakEvent, honours cancellation, then ForgeEventFactory.doPlayerHarvestCheck). Every lens placement or conversion posts ForgeEventFactory.onBlockPlace(fakePlayer, BlockSnapshot, Direction) and reverts on cancel. Phantom Breaker drops use boundPosition and the target's block entity. bb06b24a adds the playerWillDestroy call to WorldUtil.breakExtraBlock (the drill's area mining, changelog 1.3.11 'drill not dropping block contents for certain mods'), which needs the drills bundle merged first.

NeoForge EventHooks.doPlayerHarvestCheck(player, state, level, pos) becomes Forge 47 ForgeEventFactory.doPlayerHarvestCheck(player, state, state.canHarvestBlock(level, pos, player)). With one fixed profile a claim plugin has to trust [ActuallyAdditions] for machines to work inside claims. critic_notes:
Critic review of the Actually Additions inventory (read only, nothing written to the repo). I checked it against the vendored base in ports/actuallyadditions, the four upstream worktrees under bp2/up, the Arclight common.jar, the Forge 47.4.0 sources and the pack index. Total is now 264.5 h in 14 bundles (was 261.5 h in 13). Every one of the 551 non merge upstream commits after 97532ff is still named in a bundle spec or an exclusion (re-checked with git rev-list against the inventory text, 0 missing).

Corrections of fact:
- The setup stage already did most of fork-baseline-version: mod_version, jar name, reproducible jar c37140ce, LICENSE_actuallyadditions and NOTICE_actuallyadditions, and the mods.toml license fields (1eccbee3, a6bcde14). That leaves the optional deps, pack.mcmeta pack_format 6 (should be 15), the live invtweaks annotation package (split package risk), .cache and ThreadSpecialFetcher. 2 h became 1.5 h.
- Mixins: Forge 47 does not read [[mixins]] in mods.toml (that is the NeoForge form main uses). Use the MixinConfigs manifest attribute, pin MixinGradle 0.7.38 and the 0.8.5 annotation processor, as ports/enderio, spiced-twilight and littletiles do. Patchouli has to be the full jar at compile time, because PageReconstructor and PatchouliPages use internal Patchouli client classes. Arclight's RepairContainerMixin only touches AnvilMenu.createResult, so AnvilMixin is safe (javap checked).
- baseline-boot-smoke: 9ec20f48 and 758001e2 do not apply, since the base already uses RegisterParticleProvidersEvent and DistExecutor. Only f9897f06 applies: ClientRegistryHandler has mod bus listeners on the Forge bus (ActuallyAdditionsClient.java:97). Per the task, the OLD jar is the vendored base build c37140ce unless the base needs boot fixes.
- menu-open-and-validity: f2596f97 and 82aaacf1 are no-ops on the base (NetworkHooks.openScreen already gets the pos, and getBlockPos() is worldPosition). Both are moved into the exclusions.
- 74982c36 (StopDrop) returns a BlockState from playerWillDestroy. On 1.20.1 that method returns void, so a getDrops based translation was added.
- The Patchouli book has five entries: intro, guide, tutorial, crystals and engineer_house, plus the getting_started category. The old text listed four entries.
- The lang rule was inverted. All eight 1.12 .lang files get deleted.
- The main house NBT was confirmed to carry StopDrop 1 and the 1.21 inventory compound form. The 1.20.4 house file predates aa013e84 and 19a060b3.

New local findings:
- Packet handlers: DATA_HANDLERS serves both directions. A client can send the index of a client only handler, which hits a stripped @OnlyIn method on the dedicated server and runs client code on a LAN host. The firework box stores raw slider numbers (clamp to main's GUI ranges). The XP solidifier lacks a lower bound on the button id. PLAYER_DATA_TO_SERVER is a no-op after c8e90aef. Exceptions in enqueueWork are swallowed silently. KubeJS cannot inject serverbound packets, so the test uses a dev only client command.
- Drill upgrade dupe: ContainerDrill writes the upgrades to whatever hotbar slot is selected at close (ContainerDrill.java:130-136). A client that changes the selected slot by packet duplicates them. Fixed in menu-open-and-validity.
- SYNC_PLAYER_DATA uses context.getSender() on the client, which is always null, so player data never syncs.
- Vertical digger: the base sentinel -1/0 breaks below Y 0. Main's 738f098b resets every digger at each chunk load. Use an additive marker key instead.
- 38d6404b adds a block state property persistent to all crops (additive, needs blockstate variants). The savegame note was missing.
- The compat mining lens sets for five mods that are not in the pack need their 1.20.1 ids checked, or they stay out.
- AlmostUnified does rewrite the Mekanism and IE ore outputs of the compat mining lens recipes to Thermal ores. That is expected, and the earlier claim that AU unifies nothing of AA is corrected.
- The c: to forge: tag table is now written out in full in tags-forge, so specs can be ported blindly.
- sky_void check confirmed: it is only in sky_floaters and two Dungeons Arise tags. The black quartz and plant placed features keep main's minecraft:biome filter.
